tests.description: Issue 28: the casts of the enum operands to unsigned int (the enum's compatible type, CIL ekind) are conversions between identical integer kinds and get no proof obligation (previously two cast POs proven by the enumeration-membership rule, 8 safe)
Issue #79, CodeHawk-C
Issue #76, CodeHawk-C
False-positive stack-address-escape: local array used as scratch buffer via value-parameter pointer; address cannot escape since s is passed by value, not char**
Open signed-to-signed-cast obligations due to missing bitwise-OR range propagation: xop_2_numexpr treats XBOr as RANDOM; with Option A fix, lb->safe (C>=safelb), ub->violation (C>safeub)

False-positive signed-to-unsigned-cast-ub: caste(uint16_t, X) where X > 65535 is not modelled as modular truncation; the un-truncated int value propagates into the OR and exceeds uint16_t max; byte_swap_lo (val=31) is correctly safe because 31<<8=7936 fits in uint16_t without truncation (safe 52 -> 58: issue 29 adds non-negative(E1) and int-overflow(E1, E2, op:shiftlt) for the signed (promoted) shifts, all safe)

Binary search index-upper-bound precision gap: interval widening overestimates k's range (buggy j=N gives k in [0,6]; fixed j=N-1 gives k in [0,5]); both produce open POs because the relational invariant i<=j cannot be expressed in the interval domain; violation only detectable via direct constant OOB access (fold_search_oob_step); safe 63 -> 65, open 4 -> 2: the interval quotient bound used numerical ceiling, which returned n + 1 for an integer n ((0 + 8) / 2 gave [0, 5]); the fixed search (j = N-1) now has k in [0, 4] and its index-upper-bound POs are safe

Cross-function heap invariant gap: ivec_set accesses v->data after a bounds check but carries 6 open POs (not-null, valid-mem, in-scope, lower-bound, upper-bound, ptr-upper-bound-deref) because the analyzer has no model for the postcondition of ivec_create (data is non-null and size(data)==size); inspired by bmp_set_pixel in libbmp with 13 open POs on pixels[x][y] for the same root cause

R8: initialized-range discharge handler has no transfer functions for (A) scalar assignment -- uint16_t val=42; fwrite(&val,...) -- (B) struct-copy -- pair_t p=*src; fwrite(&p.a,...) -- or (C) memset -- memset(buf,0,n); fwrite(buf,...); in all three cases the byte range is provably initialized but the handler lacks the scalar->range, struct-copy->field-range, and memset->range rules

R9: no-overlap discharge handler does not use allocation-site disjointness; fwrite generates no-overlap(buf, fp) for its two arguments; when buf is a stack variable and fp is from fopen (different allocation origins: stack vs heap), or buf is from malloc and fp is from fopen (two distinct call sites), they cannot overlap but the handler does not apply the disjoint-allocation rule

R11: not-zero false positive on static const divisors -- CodeHawk models static const variables as opaque globals of unknown value, even when their initializers are compile-time constant expressions; every division or modulo by such a constant produces an open not-zero PO; as a side effect, int-overflow is also open for signed division (INT_MIN / -1 cannot be ruled out when the divisor is unknown); no int-overflow PO is generated for % -- this is consistent with C99 (S6.5.5p6 only says the constraint (a/b)*b+a%b==a holds when the quotient is representable, leaving % behavior unspecified when it is not) but would be a missing PO under C11 (S6.5.5p6 adds: otherwise the behavior of both a/b and a%b is undefined); three depth levels: literal initializer, one-level product, two-level product; contrast: #define macros ARE treated as literals and discharge not-zero

R10: argv discharge handler uses argc#init (unconstrained formal-parameter value) when composing multiple path guards; after if(argc==0)return then inside if(argc<3), argc is in [1,2] so argv[0] should be valid, but the handler cannot derive 0 < argc#init from the compound constraint; single-guard paths work (argv[1] and argv[2] after the outer guard are safe); 6 open POs for argv[0] (null-terminated, initialized-range, not-null, initialized, ptr-upper-bound, valid-mem), 2 violations from atoi addition overflow

Analyzer and parser (CIL) word size taken from the parse platform (-m64, LP64): memcpy of 8 bytes into uint64_t, unsigned long, and char[sizeof(long)] is safe; unsigned long -> unsigned int cast stays open (no type-range proof); 3 open initialized-range on {0}-initialized local buffers

Same source parsed with -m32 (ILP32): memcpy of 8 bytes into unsigned long (4 bytes) and into char[sizeof(long)] (CIL folds sizeof(long) = 4 with the 32-bit machine model) are ptr-upper-bound violations; uint64_t copy stays safe

Unsigned 64-bit constants >= 2^63 (0xffffffffffffffffUL, 0x8000000000000000UL) are stored as negative int64 with an unsigned ikind; the analyzer must read them as 2^64 - 1 and 2^63, so that arr[x] is an index-upper-bound violation (previously proven safe with x = -1)

Issue 22: a violation requires the property to fail on every execution or a witness; interval bounds that violate the property need not be attained. (char)ch, memset with int n, x / d with unsigned d, and an i <= 10 loop index are open or delegated (previously violations once parameter type ranges are known); n == -1 in always_negative is a real violation (2)

Issue 21: integer conversions are reduced modulo 2^N (unsigned targets; GCC semantics for out-of-range signed targets), _Bool conversion gives 0/1; (uint16_t)-1 indexes out of bounds (violation), (int)(2^32+3) == 3 and (_Bool)2 == 1 index in bounds (safe); (int32_t)0xc400000aU is folded to -1006632950, so the s >= 0 branch is unreachable: its proof obligations stay open with an unreachable diagnostic (issue 25; previously index-lower-bound(s) was a violation and index-upper-bound(s) safe from the facts of other domains); the failing cast POs are implementation-defined (signed targets, C11 6.3.1.3p3) or value-wrap-around (unsigned targets, 6.3.1.3p2) rather than violations (issue 15, Part A); the remaining violation is the out-of-bounds index

Issue 21: unsigned +, -, *, unary - and integer conversions nested in expressions, conditions and PO arguments are reduced modulo 2^N; index_wrap, rhs_wrap, neg_wrap are index-upper-bound violations (previously safe with index -1), mult_wrap has b == 0 (previously two false violations with b == 2^32; return arr[b] is unreachable and its POs stay open, issue 25), cast_cond: (uint8_t)x is no longer the identity in the symbolic-sets translator (it made the reachable arr[x - 291] unreachable and initialized(x) open), nowrap stays safe, param_index_wrap is safe relative to the delegated uint-underflow precondition

Issue 29: unsigned << is reduced modulo 2^N (C11 6.5.7p4); 0xF0000000u << 4 == 0 and 2^63 << 1 == 0 (64-bit) give not-zero violations (previously safe with v == 2^36 * 15), shl_nowrap stays safe, shl_maywrap and shl_var are open, 2^61 << 2 == 2^63 is folded exactly (xsimplify previously overflowed the OCaml int)

Issue 29: signed E1 << E2 (C11 6.5.7p4) gets non-negative(E1) and int-overflow(E1, E2, op:shiftlt); 1 << 31, k << 1 with k == 2^30 are int-overflow violations, -1 << 1 and k << 2 with k == -3 are non-negative(E1) violations (non-negative checker now reports a universal violation when the upper bound is negative); bounded operands (k < 1000, uint8_t b < 128 promoted, variable shift amount, 64-bit) are safe; unbounded operands are delegated, and the call deleg(1 << 29) violates the delegated condition (SPO); unsigned << gets no int-overflow PO; (int)p[0] << 8 for uint8_t *p without invariant is safe by the range of uint8_t (open: initialized(p[0]), initialized(p[1]))

Issue 29: e1 >> k (constant k, 0 <= k < N) is floor(e1 / 2^k) (C11 6.5.7p5; GCC arithmetic shift for negative signed e1), translated as e1 DIV 2^k for e1 >= 0 and (e1 - (2^k - 1)) DIV 2^k for e1 < 0; previously only k <= 4 was translated and numerical ceiling of an integer was one too high; u >> 5 with u >= 32 is not-zero safe, -9 >> 3 == -2 gives a not-zero violation, s >> 2 for s in [-100, -1] is not-zero safe; shr_bound_ceil is index safe since interval DIV truncates (issue 31b, was open); the variable shift amount is open

Universal uint-underflow violation of e1 - e2 requires UB(e1) - LB(e2) < 0 (the checker used UB(e2)): a in [10, 20], b in [0, 100] is delegated to the api (previously a violation); a <= 20, b >= 30 is a violation

Issue 32: C / truncates toward zero and % has the sign of the dividend (C11 6.5.5p6); -7 / 2 == -3 and -7 % 4 == -3 give not-zero violations (previously folded Euclidean: -4 and 1, safe); x % 4 for x in [-10, 10] is in [-3, 3]: index-lower-bound open (previously [0, 3], safe); x % 10 for x in [0, 100], x in [-100, -1] (+ 9), unsigned u % 10, and x % 1000 for x in [0, 5] index safely; x / 4 >= 0 iff x >= -3 (previously rewritten to x >= 0): not-zero(x + 1) open; x / 4 < 0 iff x <= -4: not-zero(x + 2) safe; x / 4 <= 0 and x / 4 > 0 index safely; int-overflow(x, c, op:mod) with a constant c > 0 is safe (C11 6.5.5p6: a % b is undefined iff a / b is; previously no CheckValid case for Mod); the r += ... accumulations in the loops are open

Issue 31b: interval DIV is truncating division (C11 6.5.5p6), exact at the corners for a divisor interval excluding zero (previously floor/ceiling); x / 2 and x / d for x in [-7, 9], d in [2, 3] are in [-3, 4], x / d for x in [-9, 7], d in [-3, -2] is in [-3, 4], u / 16 for u <= 100 is <= 6: all index POs safe (previously open); x / 16 for x in [-15, -1] is 0: not-zero violation (previously open); x / 16 for x in [-16, -1] is in [-1, 0]: not-zero open; int-overflow(x, d, op:div) with a variable divisor is open (issue 34: div_checker is a stub)

Issue 28: casts from/to an enumerated type are integer conversions from/to its compatible type (CIL ekind; C11 6.7.2.2p4), with corrections and the integer cast POs (previously no correction and a cast PO proven by enumeration membership); (unsigned char)M with M = -1 is 255: index-upper-bound and cast-lb violations; (enum sgn)4294967295u is -1: not-zero violation, int-overflow safe; delegated cast bounds; the enumeration-membership cast PO of (enum sgn)u is open

Issue 27 (a): a store into a bit-field of width w reduces the value modulo 2^w into the field's range (unsigned [0, 2^w-1]; signed [-2^(w-1), 2^(w-1)-1], gcc); f:3 = 9 stores 1 (index safe, previously violation), f:3 = 8 stores 0 (not-zero violation, previously safe), g:4 = 12 stores -4 (index-lower-bound violation), f:3 = u is in [0, 7]; bit-field promotion to int (27 (c)) not covered

Issue 36: objects addressed by an argument of a callee without known side effects are abstracted at the call (the addressed sub-object, or the enclosing array for a pointer to an array element, with all its fields and elements); previously only &lval/array arguments themselves were abstracted (only the variable for lval): (void *)&c, p = &v; f(p), the fields of &s, and (void *)buf kept their values, so index-upper-bound(x) was proven safe with x == 0 although the callee may make x == 12 (now open: void_out, ptr_copy, struct_out, array_out; field_out was already open); field_sibling: since issue 45, s.b is abstracted as well (open): the address of s escapes to ext_int, and a pointer to the first member, converted, points to the structure (C11 6.7.2.1p15)

Issue 35: an access whose type differs from the type of the accessed object has an unknown value (read) or abstracts the object (write): *(char *)&e was the int e itself, so pun_read proved its branch unreachable and index-upper-bound(x) safe with x == 0 (12 on x86-64), now open; pun_write: index bounds of e open (previously violation/safe with e == 12). Pointer arithmetic on a known address shifts the last index instead of appending one, and keeps the field offset: ptr_plus_write *(p + 1) = 12 with p = &a[0] writes a[1] (index-upper-bound(a[1]) violation, previously safe with a[1] == 0); ptr_plus_field (p + 1)->a == 0 safe, (p + 1)->b == 12 violation (previously both open). External memory reached through void * is typed by the access (void_arg_state: uint-underflow safe). Issue 37: in the symbolic-sets domain a type-inconsistent access is no longer the object itself, so initialized(*(char *)&e) in pun_read is open (precision loss: the domain cannot distinguish the read from a partial write)

Issue 36(d): a call may modify any global (address-taken or not) unless a contract protects it (const global-variable contract, or XPreservesValue of the global in the callee's side effects/postconditions); an unresolved indirect call abstracts its lhs, argument regions and all globals (previously the call was omitted); previously callback_global, direct_global, global_field, addr_taken_global, indirect_lhs and indirect_global proved index-upper-bound safe with index 0 (now open); library_call (strlen has a summary) and local_unaffected stay safe

Issue 40: uint-underflow(e1, e2, minusa) requires a relation between the operands (LB(e1) >= UB(e2), or e2 == 0); previously a non-negative lower bound on e1 alone was accepted, so lb_first_only (no bound on b) and lb_first_ub_too_large (a >= 5, b <= 6) were proven safe (now open); bounded_both, second_zero and constant_second stay safe. Operands are return values of an external function, so the POs cannot be delegated

Issues 36(c), 37: symbolic domains. Symbolic-sets conditions: lvals without a variable were the same temporary (conditions are translated outside a transaction), so G.ptr->cnt >= G.ptr->max was TRUE, the else branch dead and initialized(x) proven safe after the join (uninit_after_condition, now open). Numerical: the field offset of (gq + 1)->a through the initial value of a global pointer was dropped, so a and b were one variable (ptr_plus_fields: index-upper-bound violation, now safe). Sym_pointersets: calls without summary now abstract out-parameter regions, globals, and the lhs of unresolved indirect calls (out_param, global_pointer, indirect_lhs: branches r != 0 were dead in that domain; statuses unchanged). partial_init: a one-byte write through (char *)&e was recorded as an assignment of e (initialized(e) safe, now open)

Issue 42: library summaries now list a block-write side effect for every pointer the function writes (58 summaries had a deref-write precondition but no write side effect; memset, read, time recorded the write only as initialization; strtok was marked functional; sscanf had no formatted-input; ioctl had no parameters): previously the written object kept its value and index-upper-bound(x) was safe with x == 0 in the nine write_* functions (now open). A block write through a null pointer, an absent variadic argument, or a non-pointer argument has no effect (guarded_args: safe). initialized(buf[0]) after buf[0] = 0; snprintf(buf, ..) is safe (the byte-sequence violation rule of the initialized checker was removed)

Issue 41: in a function with gotos the last statement of the body was translated outside the CFG, so a backward goto in the last statement was lost and its target unreachable (goto_backward: all POs at the target open, now index-upper-bound(12) violation and initialized(x) safe; goto_backward_init: initialized(x) safe). In a nested goto block a break/continue of an enclosing loop or switch fell through to the statement after the block: index-upper-bound in nested_break, nested_continue and nested_switch_break was safe (now open); inner_loop_break (break within the block) stays safe

Issue 25: a proof obligation at a location that some domain proves unreachable stays open with an explicit unreachable diagnostic (reported separately); it is not checked against the other domains' facts (previously plain_const index-lower-bound(s) was a violation and index-upper-bound(s) safe from the linear-equalities fact s == -5, and param_dead delegated both index proof obligations to the api from pepr facts); statement-local checks still apply (stmt_valid_dead: arr[3] safe); reachable code is unaffected

Issue 15 (Part A): a failing proof obligation gets the status of the resulting behavior: violation (undefined behavior: ub_index), implementation-defined (unsigned-to-signed-cast, signed-to-signed-cast-lb/ub; C11 6.3.1.3p3) or value-wrap-around (uint-overflow, uint-underflow, signed-to-unsigned-cast-lb/ub, unsigned-to-unsigned-cast; C11 6.2.5p9, 6.3.1.3p2); previously all seven were violations. All proof obligations are checked at every level; the level only selects what the reports show

Issue 43: consolidated status of the primary proof obligations (chkc report, section Consolidated status); the status of each proof obligation is unchanged. Delegated index proof obligations: read_static and rec_a/rec_b (mutual recursion, greatest fixpoint) proven via their safe call sites; read_extern (external linkage) and read_addr (address taken) trust-ext; read_open dep-open (open call-site proof obligation); read_bad upper bound dep-fail (violated call-site proof obligation; its lower bound proven); lib_post: proven (memset preserves-all-memory from its library summary; C standard library summaries are part of the analyzer's model); attr_post: 2 valid-mem proof obligations trust-lib (preserves-all-memory from the pure attribute of the external function ext_pure)

Issue 43, closed-program mode (chkc report --closed-program --entry-point main --entry-point lib_entry): external linkage alone does not imply unseen callers; read_called (external linkage, safe call site) proven; read_uncalled (no callers) uncalled, not proven (unreachability policy); lib_entry (declared entry point) and read_addr (address taken) trust-ext. Without --closed-program all eight delegated proof obligations are trust-ext

Issue 45: a call without library summary may change memory it does not receive as an argument: external memory (through pointer parameters, return values, pointers stored in memory) and locals whose address escaped (syntactic flow-insensitive escape analysis), also through pointers stored in an argument (depth 2: readv, struct field). The 14 index POs of ext_param, ext_param_defined, ext_return, escaped_call, escaped_defined, depth2_library, depth2_struct were proven safe with stale values and are open now; local_kept, local_library_arg (address only passed to memset) and ext_param_library (memset has a summary) stay safe. The violation is stack-address-escape (gx = &x) in escaped_defined

Issue 15 (Part A): verification report (chkc c-project verification-report). Boundary: ext_value and ext_ptr unmodeled (2 call sites), one indirect call (fp), memset summarized, one function with external callers assumed (program_postcondition: valid-mem(p)). Open proof obligations by remedy: call-site (index POs of lookup, open supporting POs at the call with ext_value()), external-condition (*ext_ptr(): not-null and initialized of the return value of ext_ptr), program-postcondition (valid-mem(p) after prog_fn: preserves-all-memory), global-state (g_arr[g_idx], fp), unclassified 2. Findings: a[10] violation, (int)u implementation-defined
expected-findings: 1 violation (undefined behavior on every execution reaching the
- 12 proof obligations are open; any of them may be a further violation

tests.description: Issue 50: an lval with a non-constant index does not denote a single location: a read is unknown, a condition on it constrains nothing, and a write may change every element of the same array but not other fields of the same struct. Previously all a[i] shared one variable that was read and constrained as a single value (exit_fact_after_decrement, from bzip2 mainSimpleSort: incs[hp] >= bigN survived hp--, pepr made the deref of ptr unreachable), an element accessed through a pointer was named by its index expression and kept its facts after i++ (element_after_increment: unreachable), and a write to s->buf[i] did not change s->buf[0] (write_changes_same_field: unreachable); 18 primary POs were at unreachable locations, now 0. write_keeps_other_field: both index bounds of s->buf[s->n] stay safe; write_changes_constant_element: the index bounds of garr[a[0]] are open

Issue 51: in sym_pointersets a pointer copied from a value that may be null keeps the null region. Previously f = (F *)b (b a pointer parameter, from bzip2 BZ2_bzWriteClose64) and f = (F *)n (unknown value) made f == NULL infeasible: the then-branch, including the reachable write through err, was unreachable (10 primary POs), now 0. The open PO is the integer-to-pointer cast

tests.description: Issue 3: strncpy reads its source up to and including the null character, at most n (C11 7.24.2.4p2); summary precondition deref-read(s2, min(n, nullterminator-pos(s2) + 1)): string literals shorter than n are safe, directly and through a delegated (min-length) api condition; a non-terminated fixed-size field with n equal to its size is safe

Issue 52: a string literal's array has strlen + 1 initialized elements (C11 6.4.5p6) and ptr-upper-bound allows one past the end (6.5.6p8): memcpy(buf, "abc", 4) is safe; memcpy(buf, "abc", 5) violates ptr-upper-bound and initialized-range

Contracts from attributes on application functions (codehawk branch attributeassumptions, cCHFileContract.get_application_function_attributes): a returns_nonnull postcondition is a conjecture, checked by a return-site supporting proof obligation and assumed by the callers' primary proof obligations. get_state: return-site not-null proven (address of a global element); find_state: one return site proven, one open (result of an external function without summary), callers still assume the postcondition (dependency on an open conjecture); lead_state: leading attribute attached by CIL to the base type (analyzer issue #59), no postcondition, caller not-null open. Other open primary proof obligations: initialized((*s).count) in the three callers, stack-address-escape of the external result returned by find_state. The literal return NULL case is left out because of analyzer issue #60 (null pointer constant proven not-null)

Contracts from companion specification files: the sources have no attributes; the parse step appends to the .i the preprocessed companions under cch_contracts: the header companion companion_postconditions.chk.h (of the included project header; returns_nonnull on the static inline accessor hdr_state) and the file companion companion_postconditions.c.chk.h (returns_nonnull on get_state and find_state). hdr_state, get_state: return-site not-null proven; find_state: one return site proven, one open (external result); callers of the three assume the postcondition (not-null proven); other_state has no companion entry, caller not-null open. Other open primary proof obligations: initialized((*s).count) in the four callers, stack-address-escape of the external result returned by find_state

Issues 62 and 66: specifications of external functions from attributes, exported by the analyzer (<file>_xc.xml) and classified by the verification report per axis. Complete (effects and preconditions declared; preconditions only by chkc_ attributes, user decision 2026-11-22): ext_full (chkc_preserves_all_memory; chkc_nonnull), ext_none (chkc_preserves_all_memory; chkc_requires_none), ext_unknown (chkc_effects_unknown; chkc_requires_none). Partial, listed as missing information: ext_len (pure gives effects; gcc nonnull is used but does not declare preconditions), ext_div (const gives effects only), ext_printf (gcc format: no declared axis), ext_exit (noreturn: neither). Unmodeled: ext_plain. Standard library: strlen

Verification pass (system-boundary guarantees): functions declared chkc_exported have their postconditions checked by primary proof obligations at return sites (PPOguarantee). get_s: 1 guarantee proven, declared side effect reported as not checked; find_s: 2 guarantees, 1 proven, 1 open (external lookup without specification; remedy external-condition); read_x: chkc_nonnull(1) assumed, dereference proven; local_s (not exported): 2 return-site supporting proof obligations, 1 proven, 1 open

Issue 60: a null pointer constant converted to a pointer (literal 0, NULL, via void *, via a pointer typedef) is a violation of not-null instead of an absolute address (5 violations, including the return site of an exported function that guarantees returns_nonnull); a nonzero constant is an absolute address (safe); an integer variable converted to a pointer is not evidence of non-null (delegated to the callers, or open)

Verification pass, interface preconditions: an exported function (chkc_exported) can delegate only its declared preconditions; other conditions stay open as missing preconditions (remedy missing-precondition: sum needs not-null(q), initialized(p->x), initialized(q->x)); a proof obligation discharged by a declared precondition is trust-interface; calls to the exported function in its own file check the declared precondition by primary proof obligations (proven for &g, violation for a null pointer) and get no call-site supporting proof obligations

Issue 73: out-parameter postconditions with an error discriminator (framed as library-summary postconditions / error-postconditions, mutually exclusive outcomes). chkc_initializes(i) makes the scalar leaves of *arg i initialized (post-initialized symbol); with chkc_error_returns_lt/eq(c) only in the success outcome, resolved against the interval of the call's return-value variable at the proof obligation. Proven (contract): use_checked, use_checked_ge, use_val (unconditional), use_eq_zero, use_nested (2). Open: use_unchecked (error outcome not excluded), use_error (error branch), use_plain (no postcondition), use_reassigned (status overwritten: the condition is on the return value, not on the status variable), use_eq (!= -1 not expressible as an interval), use_join (imprecise: the path without the call leaves the return value unconstrained), use_join_error, use_loop, use_prior_partial (initialized before the call on one path only), and 2 arithmetic proof obligations in use_nested. Error outcome: the location keeps its state before the call (copied into a prior-state augmentation variable at the call): use_prior (initialized at declaration, status ignored, as in the cFE *_VerifyCmdLength functions) is proven locally
